name: captured-output-transcript
description: Machine-readable grammar and diagnostic table for the captured_output.txt transcript format. validate_transcript.py reads every regex and every diagnostic's severity from this file; it does not hardcode them. Changing a pattern or a severity here changes what the validator accepts and what exit code it returns, without touching validate_transcript.py.

header.description: FORMAT.md's HEADER_RE, verbatim. Exactly one space after '===', one after '$', one before the closing '==='. Group 1 is the command text.

header_lookalike.description: A loose near-miss of the header shape (some run of '=' ... a literal '$' ... a run of '=') that does NOT match the strict header regex. Used only to flag lines that look like a botched header attempt (wrong spacing, missing space, tabs) so they are not silently swallowed into a record's body or into preamble. Any line that matches 'header' is excluded from this check first.

exit.description: FORMAT.md's EXIT_RE, verbatim. Group 1 is the (possibly negative) integer exit status. First match within a record wins; later matches in the same record are reported as informational duplicates, not errors -- FORMAT.md defines first-wins as correct behaviour, not a defect.

exit_lookalike.description: A loose near-miss of an exit assignment (wrong case, ':' instead of '=', a non-integer value, extra trailing text) that does NOT match the strict 'exit' pattern. Flagged so a typo like 'Exit=0' or 'exit=1.5' is reported precisely instead of silently producing an unexplained TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_HAS_NO_EXIT.

ran.description: FORMAT.md's RAN_RE, verbatim. Required, once, inside any record whose command is a test command.

ran_lookalike.description: A loose near-miss of the 'Ran N tests in ...' summary line (wrong case, missing count, reworded) that does NOT match the strict 'ran' pattern.

verdict.description: FORMAT.md's VERDICT_RE, verbatim. Group 1 is 'OK' or 'FAILED'. Scanned across the WHOLE file (not just inside records) for the FAILED-anywhere rule, and scanned per-record for the 'required for test commands' rule.

test_command.description: HEURISTIC, not part of FORMAT.md: a record's header command is treated as a 'test command' (triggering the Ran/verdict requirements) if this pattern matches the command text. FORMAT.md does not define how to recognise a test command; this repository's transcripts invoke tests with 'python3 -m unittest ...', so matching the literal word 'unittest' is the pattern used. See README 'Limitations' for what this misses and what it can false-positive on.

TRANSCRIPT_HAS_NO_COMMAND_RECORDS.message: no '=== $ command ===' header found anywhere in the file; the transcript has zero command records

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_HAS_NO_EXIT.message: record has no line matching the exit pattern

TRANSCRIPT_SHOWS_TEST_FAILURE.message: a FAILED verdict line is committed in the transcript

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_EXIT_MALFORMED.message: line resembles an exit=<int> assignment but does not match the strict exit pattern

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_DUPLICATE_EXIT.message: a second (or later) valid exit= line appears in this record; FORMAT.md defines first-wins, so this is not itself an error

TRANSCRIPT_HEADER_MALFORMED.message: line resembles a '=== $ command ===' header but does not match the strict header pattern

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_MISSING_RAN_LINE.message: record's command looks like a test command but has no 'Ran N tests in ' line

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_MISSING_VERDICT.message: record's command looks like a test command but has no OK/FAILED verdict line

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_RAN_LINE_MALFORMED.message: line resembles the unittest 'Ran N tests in ' summary but does not match the strict pattern

TRANSCRIPT_RECORD_VERDICT_BEFORE_RAN.message: the record's verdict line (OK/FAILED) appears before its 'Ran N tests in ' line -- unittest never prints them in that order, so this indicates the transcript was edited or corrupted after capture

TRANSCRIPT_PREAMBLE_EXIT_LOOKALIKE.message: a line matching the exit pattern (or a near miss) appears before the first header, i.e. inside preamble; FORMAT.md ignores preamble entirely, so this is informational only, typically a missing header above it

TRANSCRIPT_FILE_UNREADABLE.message: the transcript file could not be read or decoded as UTF-8
